title: zia_url_filtering_and_cloud_app_settings bypasses legacy client for PUT and returns 401

blocks.text: Legacy authentication is configured through these environment variables:
ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT=true ZIA_USERNAME= ZIA_PASSWORD= ZIA_API_KEY= ZIA_CLOUD=
Can open Zscaler Support Case if this is needed.
The relevant sequence in the log is:

blocks.item: GET /api/v1/advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings is successfully sent through the legacy ZIA client to https://zsapi.<cloud>.net.
The subsequent PUT is sent through the OneAPI client to https://api.zsapi.net/zia/api/v1/advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings.

blocks.text: N/A
When ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT=true, both the GET and PUT requests should be routed through the legacy ZIA client.
The PUT should be sent to:
https://zsapi.<cloud>.net/api/v1/advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings
Terraform should update the URL Filtering and Cloud App settings successfully.
The GET is routed correctly through the legacy client:
GET https://zsapi.<cloud>.net/api/v1/advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings
The resource then sends its PUT directly through OneAPI:
PUT https://api.zsapi.net/zia/api/v1/advancedUrlFilterAndCloudAppSettings
The request does not have valid OneAPI OAuth authorization because the provider is configured for legacy authentication. OneAPI returns:
This appears to be caused by the resource calling service.Client.ExecuteRequest(...) directly for its full-payload PUT:
https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zia/blob/v4.8.3/zia/resource_zia_url_filtering_and_cloud_app_settings.go#L299-L367
The SDK's normal UpdateWithPut method checks UseLegacyClient and dispatches through LegacyClient.ZiaClient:
https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-sdk-go/blob/v3.8.44/zscaler/ziarequests.go#L82-L90
Calling ExecuteRequest directly bypasses that legacy dispatch and constructs the api.zsapi.net OneAPI request.
export ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT=true export ZIA_USERNAME="<username>" export ZIA_PASSWORD="<password>" export ZIA_API_KEY="<api-key>" export ZIA_CLOUD="<legacy-cloud>"

blocks.item: The legacy credentials are valid because the GET for the same endpoint succeeds.
Other requests made through the legacy SDK methods are routed to zsapi.<cloud>.net.
Switching this resource to the corresponding data source works because it performs only the correctly routed GET.
A potential fix would be to add/use a raw JSON PUT helper that preserves the full payload while dispatching through the legacy client whenever UseLegacyClient is enabled.
